'''Antoine Georges''' (born 1961) is a French [[physicist]]. He is a professor at the [[Collège de France]] in [[Paris]] (where he holds the chair of Condensed Matter Physics) and the director of the Center for Computational Quantum Physics at the [[Flatiron Institute]], [[New York City|New York]]. In 2023, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230502194908/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2023-nas-election.html nasonline.org]</ref>

==Early life and education==
Georges' interest in science began during his teenage years at his father's laboratory at the [[French Institute of Health and Medical Research]].<ref name=cnrs>{{cite journal|url=http://www2.cnrs.fr/en/844.htm|title=Antoine Georges: Theorist of Condensed Matter|publisher=[[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]]|journal=CNRS International Magazine|issn=1778-1442}}</ref>
In 1983 he graduated from the [[École Polytechnique]] and joined [[École Normale Supérieure]] where he completed his PhD in 1988 ([[Pierre-Gilles de Gennes]] was the president of his PhD committee). 

==Career==
In 1989, he became a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at [[Princeton University]] in order to work on high-critical-temperature superconductors in the group of [[Philip Warren Anderson|Phil Anderson]].<ref name = cnrs/> In the Fall of 1990, he started collaborating with [[Gabriel Kotliar]] who had recently joined [[Rutgers University]] and together they developed today's formulation of [[dynamical mean field theory|Dynamical Mean Field Theory]] by mapping it onto the self-consistent solution of a quantum impurity model. He also worked with [[Anirvan Sengupta]] on [[Kondo effect]]s and performed theoretical work on [[spin glass]]es and [[quantum spin liquid]]s along with [[Olivier Parcollet]] and [[Subir Sachdev]]. He returned to Ecole Normale Supérieure in 1991 as a researcher with the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] and an adjunct professor at Ecole Polytechnique. 

In 2003, he was appointed full professor at Ecole Polytechnique and relocated there, creating a research group in theoretical condensed matter physics at the [[Centre de Physique Théorique]]. He was the chair of the physics department of Ecole Polytechnique from 2006 to 2009. In 2009, he was elected a professor at the [[Collège de France]] on the chair of condensed matter physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cpht.polytechnique.fr/cpht/correl/people/georges/homepage.htm|title=Antoine Georges|publisher=Centre de Physique Théorique|accessdate=December 22, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224180611/http://www.cpht.polytechnique.fr/cpht/correl/people/georges/homepage.htm|archive-date=2013-12-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.polytechnique.edu/accueil/l-ecole-polytechnique/prix-et-distinctions/antoine-georges-40854.kjsp |title=Antoine Georges was appointed as a teacher at the Collège de France in February 2009 |publisher=École Polytechnique |accessdate=December 22, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224100248/http://www.polytechnique.edu/accueil/l-ecole-polytechnique/prix-et-distinctions/antoine-georges-40854.kjsp |archivedate=December 24, 2013 }}</ref> 

In 2010 he was named [[Arnold Sommerfeld|Sommerfeld lecturer]] by [[LMU Munich]] and in 2011 became [[Erwin Schrödinger|Schrödinger lecturer]] at the [[ETH Zurich]]. The same year he became a part-time professor at the [[University of Geneva]] and prior to all of it, he was a recipient of the ''[[Dargelos Prize]]'' in 2004 from his alma mater. In 2006 he was awarded the ''[[Europhysics Prize]]'' in [[condensed matter]] and next year he was honoured with a [[CNRS Silver Medal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/User/Georges_Antoine|title=Antoine Georges|publisher=[[Academia Europaea]]|accessdate=December 22, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.polytechnique.edu/home/about-ecole-polytechnique/agilent-prize-32564.kjsp |title=Antoine Georges and Gabriel Kotliar were both awarded the Agilent Technologies Europhysics Prize in 2006 |publisher=École Polytechnique |accessdate=December 22, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131224111137/https://www.polytechnique.edu/home/about-ecole-polytechnique/agilent-prize-32564.kjsp |archivedate=December 24, 2013 }}</ref> He has been jointly awarded the 2022 [[Eugene Feenberg Memorial Medal|Feenberg Memorial Medal]] with [[Gabriel Kotliar]] and [[Dieter Vollhardt]] for work that has significantly advanced the field of many-body physics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Feenberg Memorial Medal awardees announced! – RPMBT 21 |url=https://tarheels.live/rpmbt21/2022/08/05/feenberg-memorial-medal-awardees-announced/ |access-date=2022-10-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>
